image_description: A grey whale is captured in the ocean, with its tail flukes raised high above the water surface as it dives. The background features a rocky shoreline. The whale's skin appears dark grey/black with some lighter mottling, and the underside of the flukes shows a lighter grey tone. Water splashes around the base of the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely submerged and not visible in the frame; only the tail flukes are shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal side of the flukes displays the characteristic dark grey/black coloration with subtle mottling consistent with grey whale skin texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal area/knuckles are submerged or outside the frame; only the tail stock and flukes are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The main body is submerged; only the tail section is visible, making full body shape assessment impossible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture on the flukes appears rough and mottled, consistent with the presence of barnacles/callosities typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Baleen plates are located inside the mouth/head, which is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the anterior body and are not visible in this tail-focused shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are clearly visible, broad, and exhibit a distinct central notch (indentation) between the two lobes. The trailing edges appear relatively smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface of the flukes shows a non-uniform, slightly bumpy texture consistent with callosities/barnacle encrustation.

artifact_observations.location: Underside of the left fluke (viewer's left)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition between the dark dorsal skin and the lighter ventral skin on the left fluke appears slightly smeared or airbrushed compared to the sharper definition on the right fluke. artifact_observations.location: Base of the right fluke where it meets the water
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point between the tail stock and the fluke seems to merge into the splash/water somewhat unnaturally. The geometry of the tail stock appears slightly flattened or distorted by the water interaction, lacking clear volumetric definition.

To audit the boundary sharpness between the whale and the water/splash, checking for melting or fusion artifacts at the contact points.
To evaluate the realism of the water dynamics and the fine-grained texture of the skin, looking for AI-generated smoothing or noise patterns.
